text:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: alert fired — service=hosted-inference, alert=high-p95-latency, severity=critical. Escalation policy 'sre-primary' attempting first contact with primary on-call carla. Link: https://pagerduty.com/alerts/PD123456

pagerduty: PagerDuty notification sent to carla (primary). No ack within 60s, escalating to secondary bob.

carla (oncall): ugh just woke up, i'm on my phone, trying to open pager but flaky wifi. can someone paste the short impact?

bob (sre): seeing p95 jump from ~120ms to ~2.1s over the last 3m on the hosted inference autoscaler pool. error rate small but timeouts spiked. curl health shows some hosts 503.

alice (product): customers on-moderate tier might see UI requests stall, some requests retrying. Not yet widespread but a few support pings.

incidentbot: Escalation proceeded: manager erin was paged after secondary ack timeout (policy had manager fallback enabled). Manager contact triggered.

erin (eng-manager): I'm awake. tagging in. what's the mitigation plan? any recent deploys?

dave (infra): rolling restart of a handful of nodes started ~7m ago for kernel patch, but that should have finished. deploying probe now to check host health across zones: ```for h in $(cat hosts.txt); do curl -sS -m 2 http://$h:8080/health || echo $h failed; done```

bob (sre): logs show `gpu0 OOM` and `inference queue slow` on 3 hosts in us-west-2. Likely a bad rollout of model-quantization change that increased memory pressure. I can revert the deploy to the last stable artifact.

carla (oncall): acking now. :white_check_mark: I'm on-call and will coordinate. repro steps?

bob (sre): thanks. rollback command (k8s): ```kubectl -n inference set image deploy/inference-service inference=image:redwood/inference:2026-04-11-stable``` doing a canary rollback to 10% then scale. will monitor p95.

erin (eng-manager): please do incremental rollback and hold traffic where possible. open incident doc and put a short blameless note. link to doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/incident/HI-2026-04-11

dave (infra): temporarily routing new requests away from those 3 hosts via `curl -X POST https://ops-api/route/remove -d '{"hosts":[...]}''` (details redacted). traffic drain in progress, LB draining: 2/3 hosts drained.

bob (sre): rollback started. canary pods up. initial p95 dropping from 2.1s -> 460ms on canary. overall cluster still noisy, but improving.

carla (oncall): update for oncall handoff: primary acked and is active, I'll stay on for next 30m then hand to next rotation if stable.

alice (product): we've alerted support and CS; they're triaging affected customers. initial impact window ~7-12m, only a handful of customers reported.

bob (sre): monitoring graphs: p95 trending down to ~150ms now. error rate back to baseline. I'll keep rollback until stable for 10m, then promote.

erin (eng-manager): good. after stabilization, pls capture root cause: quantization memory regressed on specific GPU driver + image. schedule postmortem if needed.

incidentbot: Alert resolved by automatic closure after service recovered. Final note: escalation sequence fired (primary->secondary->manager) because primary initial ack delayed; no customer-facing data loss.

carla (oncall): closing notes: root cause suspected bad quantization flag, rollback performed, LB drained unhealthy hosts, monitoring alarms reset. I'll create minimal incident summary in the doc and ping SRE for a follow-up RFC. :thumbsup:

bob (sre): leaving a quick checklist: 1) confirm kernel + driver compat 2) add memory-pressure alert earlier 3) add runbook step to prefer routing before full rollback 4) test quantization on staging with same driver.

erin (eng-manager): thanks team. good coordination. I'll mark this as an incident with manager notification and schedule a 30m post-incident review.

pagerduty: PagerDuty log: escalation policy 'sre-primary' executed; contacts paged: carla -> bob -> erin. Timings: primary ack at 45s, secondary ack at 120s, manager paged at 150s.

incidentbot: End of thread. Archive to incident channel and incident doc.
